students.title: Belly Bond
students.text: A wearable that lets partners and the social environment of a pregnant person feel the baby's movements. Two straps are worn around each person's stomach: pressure sensors in one detect the movements and send signals to the other, which simulates them in real time as light pressure or vibration, at home or on the move, even when apart.

students.title: Snooze Vest
students.text: A smart vest that prevents snoring and analyses sleep. Body sensors capture heartbeat, breathing, body temperature, movement and sleeping position; built-in vibration units wake the wearer gently, and detachable blocks help to avoid sleeping on the back. The Snooze app visualises sleep cycles and flags possible sleep apnea.

images.alt: Snooze Vest on a torso form with posters

students.title: Aura
students.text: An AI-powered medication dispenser for people with dementia and older people living independently. It dispenses medication on time, checks in daily with a comforting voice, answers questions about routines and connects with family members, helping people stay autonomous at home or in a care facility.

students.title: SHIFT
students.text: Thesis project in Industrial Design. SHIFT explores programmable matter as a sustainable and reusable design approach: one neutral block reconfigures into seating with backrest, armrests, adjustable height, inclination, length and width.
